lines: Angeline the Baker, her age was forty-three,
Should have married Angeline when she'd have married me.
Tell how I took Miss Angeline down to the county fair,
Her father chased me halfway home and told me to stay there.
Bought my love a brand new dress, neither black nor brown,
Was the color of the stormy sky, before the rain pours down.
Angeline is lovely, Angeline is tall,
She broke her little ankle bone from dancing in the hall.
Angeline the Baker, made me weep and moan,
Left me standing by myself, to play the old jawbone.
Angeline the Baker, She lived on the village green,
And the way that I love her still, beats all to be seen.
Angeline the Baker, her age is forty-three,
Little children round her feet and a banjo on her knee.
